selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech by wandering the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians by day, then stay for the spectacular transformation at dusk when food stalls fill the air with smoke and spices. Explore the labyrinthine souks of the old medina, haggling for spices, leather goods, and lanterns.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Journey to the iconic Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga for a sunset camel trek deep into the Sahara. Spend the night in a traditional Berber nomad camp under a breathtaking canopy of stars, enjoy live Gnawa drumming around a campfire, and wake before dawn to witness a golden sunrise over the dunes — one of Morocco's most unforgettable adventures.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back into Morocco's imperial past with a self-guided or local-guided tour of the stunning 19th-century Bahia Palace, adorned with intricate zellij tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush Andalusian gardens. Continue to the nearby Saadian Tombs, a hidden royal necropolis dating to the 16th century, rediscovered only in 1917 and filled with ornate marble and gold-leaf decoration.
experiences.location: Kasbah & Riad Zitoun districts, Southern Medina, Marrakech

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class led by a local chef in a traditional riad kitchen. Begin with a guided tour of the spice souks to select fresh ingredients like ras el hanout, preserved lemons, and saffron. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as chicken tagine, harira soup, and msemen flatbread, then sit down to enjoy the feast you've created with mint tea and fresh pastries.

experiences.name: Todra Gorge Rock Climbing & Gorge Hike
experiences.description: En route to or from the Sahara, stop at the dramatic Todra Gorge — towering 300-meter canyon walls carved by the Todra River. Hire a local guide for a thrilling introductory rock climbing session on the gorge walls or trek through the narrow canyon floor as the light shifts through the cliffs. The area is also a world-class destination for experienced climbers with hundreds of established routes.
experiences.location: Todra Gorge, Tinghir Province, High Atlas foothills

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara

day_by_day.morning: No activities – flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities – flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a shared petit taxi or airport bus to Aegean Bliss Resort (negotiate fare in advance, budget ~50–70 MAD). Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick snack from a 24-hour convenience kiosk near the airport or hotel reception (~20–30 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night. Do not plan any sightseeing on Day 1. Keep some Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) ready – exchange a small amount at the airport kiosk for taxi and immediate expenses. ATMs are available at the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café (mint tea, msemen flatbread, amlou almond dip – ~30–50 MAD). Head to Jemaa el-Fna Square, the beating heart of Marrakech. Explore the open-air market, watch street performers, snake charmers, and storytellers. Visit the nearby Koutoubia Mosque and gardens (exterior only, free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into the Medina's souks – wander through the labyrinthine alleyways of the spice souk, leather souk, and lantern souk. Bargain for souvenirs and textiles. Visit the free-entry Mellah (Jewish Quarter) for a slice of Marrakech's multicultural history. Stop at Place des Épices for a rooftop café break with panoramic views (~20 MAD for tea).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna at sunset when the square transforms into a massive open-air food market. Eat dinner from the street stalls – harira soup, grilled kefta skewers, and fresh orange juice (~60–80 MAD for a full meal). Stroll the square and soak in the live gnawa music and entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café – mint tea, msemen, olive oil (~30–50 MAD)
meals.lunch: Cheap tagine or couscous at a local restaurant inside the Medina (~50–70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Street food stalls at Jemaa el-Fna – harira, kefta, orange juice (~60–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the Medina streets are uneven. Keep your belongings secure in the busy souks. Bargaining is expected and part of the culture; start at 50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD) – a stunning 19th-century palace with intricate Moroccan tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush gardens. Arrive early to beat the crowds. Afterward, walk to the nearby Mellah market for fresh fruit and local produce.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD) – beautifully preserved royal tombs dating from the 16th century, adorned with Italian Carrara marble and gold leaf. Then visit the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) for sweeping views from the ramparts and a sense of the city's imperial grandeur. Take a break at a local café in the Kasbah neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Mellah neighborhood at dusk. Head back toward the Medina for dinner at a budget-friendly local restaurant. Try a slow-cooked lamb or chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives. End the night with a stroll along the lit-up walls of the old Medina.

meals.breakfast: Café near Bahia Palace – coffee, hard-boiled egg, khobz bread (~25–40 MAD)
meals.lunch: Sandwich or snack from a Medina street vendor (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near Kasbah – tagine with bread and mint tea (~70–90 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Bahia Palace, Saadian Tombs, and El Badi Palace are all walkable from each other in the southern Medina. A combined visit to all three is easily done in one day. Carry water – March can be warm during the day (~20–25°C).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure (around 07:00) on a shared group tour or budget CTM bus toward Ouarzazate and the Draa Valley. This is the start of the Sahara desert journey. The route passes through the dramatic High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m). Stop at a roadside Berber café for breakfast with mountain views (~30 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ouarzazate by early afternoon. Visit the Kasbah Taourirt (entry ~20 MAD), a UNESCO-listed mud-brick fortress and one of the finest kasbahs in Morocco. Walk through its narrow alleys and admire the traditional Berber architecture. Optionally, peek at the nearby Atlas Film Studios (exterior is free), where films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones were shot.
day_by_day.evening: Continue east toward Zagora or book a budget guesthouse in Ouarzazate (~150–200 MAD per night for a dorm or basic room). Enjoy a simple Berber dinner of lentil soup, bread, and tagine at a local auberge. Stargaze from the rooftop under remarkably clear desert skies.

meals.breakfast: Roadside Berber café in the Atlas Mountains – mint tea, bread, cheese (~30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack purchased before departure from Marrakech (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local auberge in Ouarzazate – lentil soup, tagine, bread (~60–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Marrakech–Ouarzazate–Merzouga shared transport or group tour in advance for the best budget rates (~200–350 MAD per person for shared transport). The Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass can be cold and foggy in March – bring a light jacket. Road travel takes approximately 4–5 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early from Ouarzazate toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes (approximately 5–6 hours by shared transport or group tour, ~150–250 MAD). Pass through the stunning Draa Valley with its ancient kasbahs and palmeries, the Valley of Roses near Kelaat M'Gouna, and the Todra Gorge for a short stop and short hike (~free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Merzouga village by early afternoon. Check into a budget desert camp or auberge (~200–300 MAD per night). Rest and hydrate. At around 16:00, mount a dromedary camel for a sunset camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes (included in most budget camp packages or ~150–200 MAD separately). Ride through the golden sea of sand dunes as the sun dips toward the horizon.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a desert bivouac camp as the stars emerge. Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner around a campfire – harira soup, tagine, Moroccan salads, and mint tea (~included in camp package or ~80–100 MAD). Listen to live Gnawa drumming and music under a breathtaking Saharan sky. Sleep in a traditional Berber tent.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the auberge before departure – bread, jam, coffee (~20–30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Roadside stop at a local café in the Draa Valley or Todra Gorge (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Desert camp Berber dinner around campfire – harira, tagine, mint tea (included in camp or ~80–100 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: March nights in the Sahara can be surprisingly cold (5–10°C). Bring a warm layer and sleeping bag liner. Most budget desert camps provide blankets. The camel trek at sunset is the highlight of the trip – don't miss it. Sunrise camel treks are also available the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (around 06:00) to climb the nearest sand dune and watch the Sahara sunrise – one of the most spectacular free experiences in Morocco. Take photos, meditate, or simply absorb the silence of the desert. Return to camp for a simple Berber breakfast of bread, olive oil, honey, and mint tea. Check out of the desert camp and ride camels or walk back to Merzouga village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Merzouga village on foot – visit the local market, interact with Tuareg artisans, and browse handmade desert crafts. Optionally, rent a quad bike for a thrilling desert adventure (~150–200 MAD/hour). Begin the return journey toward Ouarzazate or Marrakech via shared transport. Stop at the Draa Valley palmeries for a short walk through the oasis (~free).
day_by_day.evening: Overnight stop in Ouarzazate or push on toward Marrakech depending on energy and transport schedule. If staying in Ouarzazate, enjoy a rooftop dinner with views of the kasbah. If returning to Marrakech, arrive by late evening and grab a quick bite near the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Desert camp – bread, honey, olive oil, mint tea (included or ~20–30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Roadside café or packed snacks during transit (~30–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant in Ouarzazate or street food in Marrakech (~60–90 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return transport from Merzouga a day in advance – shared taxis and minibuses fill up quickly. The full Marrakech–Sahara–Marrakech loop is best done as a 3-day journey (Days 4–6). Carry extra water and sunscreen for the desert day.

day_by_day.morning: Back in Marrakech for a final morning. Visit the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum (garden entry ~150 MAD – a splurge worth it for the electric blue architecture, exotic cacti, and tranquil pools). Designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent, it is one of Morocco's most iconic gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks – pick up argan oil, Moroccan leather goods, spices, or handmade ceramics. Visit the Musée de Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) for a final dose of Moroccan art and history housed inside a stunning 19th-century palace. Enjoy a final mint tea at a rooftop café overlooking the Medina.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a mid-range local restaurant – treat yourself to a full Moroccan feast: bastilla (pigeon pie), lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, and chebakia pastries for dessert (~100–150 MAD). Head back to the hotel, pack up, and prepare for departure. If your flight is early the next day, arrange a pre-booked taxi the night before (~60–80 MAD to the airport).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café – msemen, amlou, mint tea (~30–50 MAD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near Majorelle Garden – Moroccan salad, khobz, fresh juice (~50–70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Farewell Moroccan feast at a local restaurant – bastilla, tagine, chebakia (~100–150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden can get crowded after 10:00 – arrive right at opening time (09:00) for the best experience. Keep some Dirhams for airport tips and last-minute purchases. Exchange any leftover MAD back to your home currency at the airport. Average 7-day budget estimate: ~2,500–3,500 MAD (~$250–$350 USD) excluding flights and accommodation, covering transport, entry fees, meals, and activities.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room. Take a short stroll around the hotel grounds to decompress after the flight.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the hotel bar or room service upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Given the late arrival, keep Day 1 stress-free. Confirm your transfer or taxi in advance. Exchange a small amount of currency (Moroccan Dirham) at the airport for tips and incidentals. Prepare a comfortable kit for the ride to the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Once refreshed, head to Djemaa el-Fna Square – the beating heart of Marrakech. Arrive mid-morning to explore the square as vendors and storytellers set up. Walk through the adjacent Souks of Marrakech, browsing spice stalls, leather goods, lanterns, and textiles. Hire a local guide (~150–200 MAD) for a 1.5-hour medina orientation walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with ornate tilework and lush gardens. Afterward, walk to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) to explore its narrow alleys and historic synagogues. Stop at the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD) for a fascinating glimpse into royal Moroccan history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna at dusk when it transforms into a spectacular open-air carnival with musicians, acrobats, snake charmers, and food stalls. Climb to a rooftop café terrace overlooking the square for mint tea and the magical atmosphere. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the medina.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet – enjoy Moroccan staples like msemen (flatbread), amlou (almond-argan dip), fresh juices, and coffee
meals.lunch: Café des Épices near the spice square – try a tagine or a Moroccan salad plate (80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Le Jardin restaurant in the medina – beautiful courtyard setting, traditional Moroccan cuisine; lamb tagine or bastilla recommended (150–220 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the medina has uneven cobblestones. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) out of cultural respect. Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at 40–50% of the asking price. Stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a visit to the Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD), the iconic cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Explore the Berber Museum on-site. Afterward, walk to the nearby Yves Saint Laurent Museum (entry ~100 MAD) for a cultural detour into fashion and art inspired by Morocco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Koutoubia Mosque and its gardens – the minaret is the most iconic landmark in Marrakech (non-Muslims admire the exterior). Then visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), a breathtaking 14th-century Islamic college with exquisite stucco carvings, cedar woodwork, and zellige tilework. Spend time exploring the Mouassine neighborhood and its artisan workshops.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional hammam experience at a mid-range local hammam such as Hammam de la Rose or Hammam Bab Doukkala (~200–350 MAD including scrub and massage). Afterward, enjoy a calm dinner near the Gueliz district (Marrakech's modern quarter).

meals.breakfast: Café Arabe near the medina – fresh pastries, Moroccan crepes (beghrir), and café au lait (60–90 MAD)
meals.lunch: Nomad Restaurant – rooftop dining with panoramic views; try the Moroccan burger or slow-cooked lamb (120–180 MAD)
meals.dinner: Kechmara in Gueliz – a lively bistro blending Moroccan and international flavors; relaxed atmosphere, great cocktails (150–200 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book Majorelle Garden tickets online in advance to avoid long queues – it is one of Morocco's most visited sites. The hammam experience is a must-do cultural ritual; book ahead for evening slots. Gueliz is walkable or a short petit taxi ride from the medina (~20–30 MAD).

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (around 7:00–8:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert – this is a long but spectacular driving day (~9–10 hours total with stops). Travel southeast through the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka Pass (2,260m elevation). Stop at Aït Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage Site – an ancient fortified ksar (village) used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the ksar on foot with a local guide (~1 hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving through the Draa Valley and the rose-growing town of Kelaat M'Gouna. Pass through Boumalne Dadès and the dramatic Dadès Gorge for a short scenic stop and photos. Continue toward Erfoud and then Merzouga – the gateway to the Erg Chebbi dunes of the Sahara.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Merzouga by late afternoon or early evening. Mount camels (or opt for a 4x4) for a 45-minute sunset ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes – one of the most awe-inspiring experiences in Morocco. Arrive at your desert camp, watch the sunset over the dunes, enjoy traditional Berber music around a campfire under a canopy of stars.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure – pack snacks and water for the road
meals.lunch: Restaurant Chez Mimi at Aït Benhaddou or a roadside café in Ouarzazate – Berber omelette, harira soup, and fresh bread (80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp – slow-cooked lamb or chicken tagine, couscous, fresh salads, and mint tea served under the stars (included with most camp bookings or ~150–200 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private driver or join a shared tour for this journey – it is the most practical option. Cost for a private driver round-trip: ~1,200–1,800 MAD. Book a mid-range desert camp in advance (e.g., Luxury Nomad Camp or similar) – expect a Berber tent with basic but comfortable amenities. Bring a warm layer as desert nights drop significantly in March (can reach 5–10°C). Sunrise over the dunes is unmissable – set an alarm.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) and climb the nearest dune for a spectacular Sahara sunrise – arguably the highlight of the entire trip. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast. Optionally, try sandboarding on the dunes (boards available at most camps, ~50–80 MAD). Explore the edge of the dunes and the Merzouga village on foot or by quad bike (~200–300 MAD for 1 hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey to Marrakech via a different scenic route through the Ziz Valley and Todra Gorge. Stop at Todra Gorge – towering 300m limestone canyon walls with a river running through; take a 30-minute walk along the gorge floor. Continue through Tinghir and back toward the Atlas Mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by late evening (approximately 9:00–10:00 PM). Check back into the hotel, shower off the desert dust, and enjoy a quiet dinner close to the hotel or room service.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Berber breakfast at the desert camp – bread, olive oil, honey, argan oil, eggs, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Auberge du Gorge at Todra Gorge – fresh trout from the river (a local specialty), salads, and tagine (100–150 MAD)
meals.dinner: Light dinner near the hotel or room service – Moroccan soup (harira), sandwiches, or a simple tagine to wind down (80–130 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The drive back is long – plan for rest stops. Todra Gorge is most dramatic in the afternoon light. If energy permits, a short hike along the gorge is highly recommended. Stay hydrated throughout the day as the desert climate is very dry. Keep sand out of electronics by using zip-lock bags.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a restful morning after the desert journey. After a late breakfast, visit the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) – a 16th-century sultan's palace now an evocative ruin with storks nesting on the ramparts; climb the walls for panoramic views of Marrakech and the Atlas Mountains. Visit the nearby Mellah Market for local produce, olives, and preserved lemons.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a cooking class at a local riad kitchen (mid-range class ~350–500 MAD per person, 3–4 hours). Learn to make traditional Moroccan dishes such as tagine, couscous, and pastilla. This is a hands-on cultural experience and you get to eat what you cook. Alternatively, explore the Tanneries of Marrakech (smaller than Fes but still fascinating) with a leather goods shop visit.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset walk along the ramparts of the medina walls – the pink-orange glow of the walls at dusk is iconic. Head to a rooftop restaurant for a farewell Marrakech dinner with views of the city skyline and the Atlas Mountains in the distance.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – slow and leisurely; try a Moroccan smoothie bowl or fresh-squeezed orange juice (famous in Marrakech)
meals.lunch: Eat what you cook in your cooking class, or grab a street food lunch near the souks – merguez sandwich, msemen with honey, fresh-squeezed orange juice (~30–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Terrasse des Épices – rooftop restaurant in the medina with beautiful views; Moroccan-inspired menu with excellent lamb dishes and vegetarian options (160–230 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance – popular classes fill up quickly. Riad Laaroussa and La Maison Arabe offer well-regarded mid-range cooking experiences. If you want a more adventurous afternoon, consider a day trip to the Ourika Valley or Atlas Mountain foothills (~30 min from Marrakech) for a Berber village walk and waterfall hike.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final Moroccan breakfast at the hotel. Spend the morning doing any last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks – argan oil, leather goods, Berber carpets, spices, and handmade ceramics make excellent gifts. Revisit Djemaa el-Fna one last time for a final cup of mint tea and to soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and head to the airport with plenty of time. Marrakech Menara Airport is approximately 15–20 minutes from the medina by taxi (~60–80 MAD). Complete check-in and security procedures. Browse duty-free for last-minute Moroccan argan products or sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Marrakech Menara Airport. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, history, desert adventure, and sensory discovery across one of the world's most captivating destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast – enjoy all your Moroccan favorites one last time: msemen, honey, amlou, fresh mint tea
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a café near the souks before heading to the airport – harira soup and Moroccan pastries (50–80 MAD), or airport dining
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Marrakech Airport, especially during peak season. Keep a small amount of MAD for last-minute purchases or tips. Declare any argan oil or food products if required by your destination country's customs regulations. Tipping is customary in Morocco: 10–15% at restaurants, 20–50 MAD for guides and drivers.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Rest and prepare for the journey ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. A private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or equivalent) awaits to whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a traditional Moroccan welcome with mint tea, rose water hand rinse, and a light late-night spread prepared by the resort. Check in, settle into your suite, and unwind.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport lounge
meals.lunch: In-flight or at departure airport
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome spread at Aegean Bliss Resort — Moroccan mezze, pastilla bites, fresh fruit, and mint tea served in your suite or the resort lounge

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm late check-in with resort. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag recovery is essential for a premium experience. Request a turndown service with aromatherapy oils for a restful first night.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a lavish breakfast at the resort. Then embark on a private guided tour of the iconic Medina of Marrakech — explore the UNESCO-listed historic quarter, winding souks, and the legendary Djemaa el-Fna square. Visit the exquisite Koutoubia Mosque gardens and the ornate Ben Youssef Medersa, a 14th-century Islamic college adorned with intricate zellige tilework and carved cedar wood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Bahia Palace, a stunning 19th-century riad palace with lavishly decorated rooms and lush courtyards. Continue to the Saadian Tombs, the beautifully preserved royal necropolis dating to the 16th century. Afterward, enjoy a curated souk experience with a personal shopping guide — discover handcrafted leather goods, Berber jewelry, argan oil products, and bespoke Moroccan lanterns.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive rooftop dinner at a premier Marrakech restaurant such as Nomad or Le Salama, offering panoramic Medina views. Savor a multi-course Moroccan tasting menu featuring bastilla au pigeon, lamb tagine with preserved lemon and olives, and saffron-infused couscous, paired with Moroccan wines or fresh-pressed juices. Return to the resort for a private hammam and massage experience.

meals.breakfast: Grand buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — Moroccan breads (khobz, msemen), fresh-squeezed orange juice, honey, argan oil, eggs, pastries, and seasonal fruits
meals.lunch: Intimate lunch at a traditional riad restaurant in the Medina — try Dar Yacout or a similarly prestigious establishment for harira soup, zaalouk, and grilled brochettes
meals.dinner: Upscale rooftop dining at Nomad Marrakech or Le Salama — Moroccan tasting menu with contemporary flair, fine Moroccan rosé or fresh juices

day_by_day.notes: Book Ben Youssef Medersa and Bahia Palace tickets in advance — early morning visits avoid crowds. Hire a licensed private guide for the Medina to ensure an authentic, hassle-free experience. Dress modestly for religious and historic sites. The hammam at the resort should be pre-booked as an evening wind-down.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, depart on a private guided excursion to the Majorelle Garden — the iconic cobalt-blue botanical sanctuary co-owned by Yves Saint Laurent, home to over 300 plant species and the Berber Museum. Follow with a visit to the adjacent Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech, a world-class fashion museum celebrating the designer's deep connection to Morocco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Palmeraie district on the outskirts of Marrakech for a private camel ride through the palm grove — a gentle taste of desert life before the grand Sahara adventure. Return to the resort for leisure time: enjoy the pool, spa, or a private cooking class with the resort chef, learning to prepare classic Moroccan dishes such as tagine, chermoula, and orange blossom desserts.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cocktail experience on the resort terrace or rooftop, followed by an immersive dinner at a luxury riad restaurant. Consider La Maison Arabe for their legendary Moroccan cuisine — slow-cooked mechoui lamb, honey-glazed pastilla, and a selection of Moroccan desserts including chebakia and orange salad with cinnamon.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at the resort with fresh pastries, amlou (almond-argan dip), and traditional mint tea ceremony
meals.lunch: Light gourmet lunch at the Majorelle Garden café or a nearby premium café — avocado toast Moroccan style, fresh salads, and cold-pressed juices
meals.dinner: La Maison Arabe or equivalent luxury riad restaurant — traditional Moroccan multi-course dinner in a romantic courtyard setting with live Gnawa music

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden opens at 8:00 AM — arrive early for a peaceful experience before tour groups arrive. The cooking class should be pre-booked with the resort. Camel ride in the Palmeraie is approximately 45–60 minutes and is suitable for all fitness levels. Confirm dinner reservations at La Maison Arabe at least 2–3 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Marrakech in a private luxury 4x4 (Land Cruiser or Range Rover) for the legendary drive to the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley route. Journey through the dramatic High Atlas Mountains, crossing the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation) with breathtaking panoramic views. Stop at a Berber village for a traditional mint tea welcome and a glimpse into mountain life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the cinematic landscapes of the Draa Valley — vast palm oases, ancient kasbahs, and red-rock desert vistas. Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou, the most spectacular ksar (fortified village) in Morocco, used as a filming location for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia. Enjoy a private guided tour of the labyrinthine mud-brick citadel with a local expert.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your luxury desert camp near Merzouga or Zagora (approximately 8–9 hours from Marrakech, with stops). Check into a premium desert glamping suite — think plush Berber tents with en-suite bathrooms, king beds, and private terraces. As the sun sets, mount camels for a golden-hour ride into the dunes. Watch the Sahara sky explode in color, then settle around a private fire for traditional Berber music, stargazing, and a lavish desert dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early power breakfast at the resort before departure — eggs, Moroccan breads, fresh juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort or a stop at a premium restaurant in Ouarzazate — Moroccan salads, grilled meats, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Romantic private dinner under the Sahara stars at the luxury desert camp — Berber tagine, couscous, grilled meats, Moroccan salads, and traditional sweets, served by candlelight with live Gnawa and Berber percussion music

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day (~8–9 hours driving with stops) — start by 7:00–7:30 AM. Ensure the private vehicle is stocked with water, snacks, and a first-aid kit. Aït Benhaddou visit is approximately 1–1.5 hours. Confirm luxury camp booking well in advance — premium camps like Scarabeo Camp, Erg Chigaga Luxury Camp, or equivalent fill up quickly. Pack layers — desert nights can be cold in March (5–10°C).

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for a private sunrise camel or quad bike ride into the Erg Chebbi or Erg Chigaga dunes — witness the Sahara awakening in shades of amber, gold, and rose. Return to camp for a lavish Berber breakfast served in your tent or on a private dune platform. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a guided nature walk with a Tuareg desert guide to learn about Saharan flora, fauna, and ancient trade routes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart the desert camp and visit a local nomadic Berber family for an authentic cultural exchange — share tea, learn about traditional desert life, and browse handcrafted goods. Continue to the Todra Gorge, a spectacular canyon with 300-meter-high rose-red cliff walls, for a scenic walk through the narrow gorge and a refreshing stop by the natural spring river.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a luxury kasbah hotel in the Draa or Dadès Valley region (such as Kasbah Tamadot, Kasbah du Toubkal, or a comparable property) for the night. Enjoy a private candlelit dinner on a panoramic terrace with sweeping valley views — slow-cooked lamb mechoui, vegetable couscous, and a traditional Moroccan dessert spread.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Berber breakfast at the desert camp — msemen pancakes, honey, argan oil, Berber omelette, dates, fresh fruit, and spiced coffee
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a local restaurant near Todra Gorge — harira, tagine, and fresh Moroccan bread with mint tea
meals.dinner: Private terrace dinner at the luxury kasbah — Moroccan multi-course menu with local wines or fresh-pressed pomegranate juice, under a canopy of stars

day_by_day.notes: Sunrise alarm at approximately 5:30–6:00 AM — worth every moment. The Todra Gorge walk is easy to moderate and takes approximately 1–1.5 hours. Confirm the luxury kasbah booking in advance. The Berber family visit should be arranged through your private guide to ensure a respectful, authentic (not staged) experience. Bring a light jacket for the gorge — it can be cool and shaded.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the kasbah before departing on the scenic return journey toward Marrakech. En route, stop at the stunning Dadès Gorge and Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) — famous for its Damask rose cultivation used in world-renowned Moroccan rose water and perfumes. Visit a rose cooperative to learn about the distillation process and purchase artisan rose products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive back through the Atlas Mountains, stopping at a traditional Berber argan cooperative where women hand-press argan oil — learn about this liquid gold and its cultural significance. Arrive back in Marrakech in the late afternoon. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort for a restorative spa session — a traditional hammam scrub, ghassoul clay mask, and a relaxing argan oil massage to recover from the desert adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Marrakech dinner at one of the city's most celebrated fine dining establishments — consider Dar Yacout, a palatial 17th-century riad offering a legendary Moroccan feast, or Al Fassia for an all-female-chef dining experience. Savor the finest expression of Moroccan haute cuisine: pigeon pastilla, saffron chicken with preserved lemon, lamb with prunes and almonds, and a spectacular dessert platter.

meals.breakfast: Full kasbah breakfast — fresh local produce, Berber breads, honey, cheese, eggs, and traditional spiced coffee
meals.lunch: Scenic roadside lunch stop in the Dadès Valley or at a premium restaurant in Ouarzazate — grilled meats, Moroccan salads, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Dar Yacout or Al Fassia Marrakech — legendary multi-course Moroccan feast in a palatial riad setting with live traditional music

day_by_day.notes: The Valley of Roses is particularly beautiful in late March/early April during the rose harvest season — timing is ideal. The argan cooperative visit supports local women's empowerment initiatives. Book the spa hammam session in advance for the late afternoon slot. Dinner reservations at Dar Yacout must be made well in advance — it is one of Marrakech's most sought-after dining experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning at leisure: take a final stroll through the Medina for last-minute souvenir shopping (spices, leather babouche slippers, handwoven textiles, or Berber silver jewelry), or relax by the resort pool with a book and fresh juice. Optional: a final visit to a local hammam for a traditional scrub and steam experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for final packing and check-out. Enjoy a farewell lunch at the resort or at a nearby upscale café. Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for your departure flight — departing with memories of ancient medinas, golden dunes, and starlit desert skies.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech. Reflect on an extraordinary 7-day journey through one of the world's most captivating destinations.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely grand breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — the full Moroccan spread with an indulgent final touch: fresh orange juice, pastries, eggs to order, and a mint tea ceremony
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at the resort restaurant or a nearby premium café — light Moroccan mezze, fresh salads, and grilled fish or chicken
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 12:00 noon — arrange a late check-out (until 2:00–3:00 PM) with the resort if your flight is in the evening. Keep some Moroccan dirhams for last-minute tips and small purchases. Ensure all artisan purchases are properly packed to avoid damage. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport procedures. A curated gift box of Moroccan argan oil, rose water, and spices makes a perfect memento or gift.
